name: smbclient
one_line: ftp-like client to access SMB/CIFS (Windows) file shares
plain: `smbclient` lets you browse and copy files on Windows file shares (SMB), from Linux, in an FTP-like prompt. It is the usual first step when nmap shows ports 139 or 445 open.
A share is a named folder offered by a server, written \\server\share or //server/share. Some shares allow anonymous (null session) access, which is a common CTF finding.
when: List the shares of a machine.
Browse a share and download files.
Upload a file to a writable share in a lab.

examples.title: List shares, no password
examples.explain: -L lists the shares and -N means no password (anonymous). Look for non-default shares and ones that are not IPC$ or ADMIN$.

examples.title: Connect with a user
examples.explain: -U user%password. Without %password it asks for it.

examples.title: Commands at the prompt
examples.cmd:
ls
cd docs
get secret.txt
exit
examples.explain: ls lists, cd changes folder, get downloads, put uploads, exit leaves. help shows all commands.

examples.title: Download a whole share
examples.cmd:
smb: \> recurse ON
smb: \> prompt OFF
smb: \> mget *
examples.explain: recurse ON goes into folders, prompt OFF stops the question for each file, mget fetches everything.

examples.title: One command and leave
examples.explain: -c runs commands separated by semicolons and quits.

examples.title: Force an SMB version
examples.explain: -m sets the maximum protocol, useful for old servers (NT1) or strict ones.

examples.title: Other helpers
examples.explain: Cross-check the share list with these tools.

mistakes: Typing the share path with single backslashes in the shell: use //server/share.
Forgetting -N and getting a password prompt for anonymous tests.
Putting a password with special characters unquoted on the command line.
Downloading with prompt ON and answering a question for every file.
Uploading files to real shares you are not authorised to change.
